title: Creating Your First GraphQL Server
description: Write your first Query and Mutation types in Hot Chocolate.

data.text: Hot Chocolate uses plain C# classes as your GraphQL types. The framework inspects these classes to build the schema automatically.
Create a `Book` type that represents a book in your system. Public properties become GraphQL fields automatically.

data.title: Book Type
data.content: A simple C# class becomes a GraphQL object type.

data.text: The `Query` type exposes read operations. Methods decorated with `[Query]` become query fields.

data.title: Query Type

data.text: Mutations modify data. Any method decorated with `[Mutation]` becomes a mutation field.

data.title: Mutation Type
data.content: Add new books to the list.

data.title: Thread Safety
data.text: This example uses a static list for simplicity. In production, use a database or thread-safe collection.
Navigate to `/graphql` in your browser to open Banana Cake Pop, Hot Chocolate's built-in IDE.

data.title: Add an Update Mutation
data.description: Extend the Mutation class with an UpdateBook method that accepts an ID and new title, then returns the updated Book.
steps: Create an UpdateBook method decorated with [Mutation]
Accept int id, string title as parameters
Find the book by ID and update its Title
data.expectedOutcome: You can run updateBook(id: 1, title: "New Title") in Banana Cake Pop and see the updated title.
